title.narrative: Pilot[Phase 1] Strengthening the humanit capacity of Jesuit Network for Migration in Central America

description.narrative: One of the main characteristics of Central America continues to be the forced displacement of people, due to the structural factors ( poverty, climate vulnerability, inequality, exclusion, generalised violence, gender-based violence, weakening of institutions and the democratic system, corruption, impunity, decrease in public social investment, among others), as well as the rise of authoritarianism and the increasingly visible impacts of climate change in different areas, especially in the Dry Corridor. In Nicaragua, the forced displacement of people since the outbreak of the socio-political crisis in 2018 has not abated. Also, in 2023, more than 500,000 migrants in transit crossed the Darién jungle and, as part of their route through Central America. It has become evident that people in situations of greater vulnerability such as women, girls and boys, LGBTIQ+, victims of torture face greater abuse during their migratory route due to State violence, organised crime and lack of information, humanitarian aid and protection services. The Jesuit Network with Migrants Central America (RJM-CA), the regional coordinating body for the social works of the Society of Jesus in Central America that provide care and accompaniment to forced migrants, as part of the direct response in each country and the reflections carried out jointly in coordination spaces and its Strategic Planning 2023-2027. 1) Strengthening the humanitarian capacity of RJM-CA members and organisational preparedness based on international standards (Sphere, CALP, IASC, etc) and developing joint guidelines and a common understanding among the network members of how to respond to forced migration. 2)Develop a case management - "humanitarian bridge" - tracking particularly vulnerable cases and offering information about services available with a rights-based perspective. 3) Developing an Alert and Response interagency mechanism.
